text:
Elena (ACME): Hey team — after three successful streaming completions our free-trial wallet still shows 500000 tokens. Calls returned 200s and responses streamed fine. Request IDs: req_abc123, req_def456, req_ghi789. Can you investigate?

Emma (support): Sorry about that — can you share account id and approximate timestamps for the calls? Also did the client set any special headers (gzip, chunking)?

Elena (ACME): account: acme-inc-4721. Timestamps ~2025-11-05T14:03:21Z, 14:04:10Z, 14:05:02Z. Client sends streaming payloads with `Content-Encoding: gzip` and uses an async retry wrapper. No idempotency-key on these calls.

Raj (eng): Noted. Two quick things we usually check: 1) whether finalize/finalize_event was emitted from the streaming proxy, 2) ledger trace for those req ids. Emma can you paste the request ids into the billing trace tool?

Emma (support): Pasted. BillingBot returned no debit entries for those req ids — ledger shows no consume event. Also, proxy logs show the stream closed with `client_disconnected` after final chunk on req_def456.

Lina (billing): If proxy never sent a finalize event to the accounting service we won't debit. We need the correlation id from proxy trace and the finalize webhook payload. Emma, can you grab the proxy correlation for req_def456?

Emma (support): Got it — proxy-cid=proxy-9982 for req_def456. Pushing logs: `proxy[9982] STREAM_END client_disconnected after 0.3s from last chunk; finalize not delivered; retry attempted`

Raj (eng): Repro steps I ran locally: streaming with gzip + network interruption + our async retry lib that replays without idempotency header can cause the proxy to mark the session closed without sending finalize to accounting. Accounting expects a single finalize call per session; missing finalize => no debit. I can repro with this minimal snippet: 

```
# simulate client: send gzipped chunks, drop connection, retry without idempotency
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams \ 
  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" \ 
  --data-binary @chunks.gz
```

Raj (eng): Root cause appears to be a race where the retry path creates a new stream-id but the original stream never completed the finalize handshake due to the connection drop. Accounting dedup relies on finalize events, not request ids, so nothing debited.

Lina (billing): Customer impact: tokens not charged (under-billed). For fairness we should (a) confirm total unbilled tokens, (b) proactively credit back if we owe them, or (c) charge if appropriate after reconciliation. Since this is a trial grant we usually credit the missing consumption back to the wallet.

Emma (support): I ran a quick token estimate from response sizes: ~154k tokens across the three streams. Proposed immediate action: (1) apply +154000 token credit to acme-inc-4721 as goodwill, (2) schedule reconciliation job to add missing ledger entries with note `retro-debit-retry-gap` if we later decide to bill. Approve?

Lina (billing): Approve the goodwill credit for trials. Please record a support ticket and tagging for finance audit. Also add `needs-ledger-patch` label for eng.

Raj (eng): I'll open a PR to: ensure finalize is sent on connection drop (best-effort), and add stronger uniqueness via idempotency header recommendation to SDKs + server-side check to close stale streams and reconcile. ETA: patch branch by EOD, patched proxy in canary tomorrow.

Emma (support): Done: credited 154000 tokens to acme-inc-4721 (support-case #S-20251105-198). Notified customer. Repro steps, proxy-cid, and logs attached in the ticket.

Elena (ACME): Thanks — appreciate the quick handling. Please confirm when the proxy fix lands so we can update our client to include idempotency keys.

Raj (eng): Will follow up tomorrow with canary results. For now: recommend client add idempotency-key for streaming requests; we'll add server-side safeguards too.

BillingBot: ledger-transaction created: tx_20251105_credit_acme_154000 (type: credit, reason: goodwill_trial_recon).

Emma (support): Closing loop for now. Reopen if you see any further anomalies, Elena. :thumbsup:
